title: A Protoretrocausal Meta-Erratum Regarding the Pending Retraction of the Anticipatory Erratum on Sappho Having Written the Dinosaurs
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: The third instrument in the erratum sequence, and the one that makes the book possible. It suspends the pending retraction of the anticipatory erratum at #1598, effective prior to that retraction's proposal, on the discovery that the erratum performed the publication whose consequences it claimed merely to anticipate: to withdraw an interpretation intelligibly, the withdrawal had to supply the interpretation in enough detail to be cited, disputed, misunderstood and independently rediscovered. THE ERRATUM WAS THE FIRST EDITION. The term protoretrocausal is glossed: proto- for the stage before the cause has been adequately formulated, retrocausal for the subsequent discovery that this stage was already consequential, meta- to indicate that responsibility has been transferred to the apparatus — and the term is explicitly not a claim about physical time but about the administratively familiar circumstance in which a later document determines what an earlier document will always have meant. The date remains unchanged; the past acquires a footnote. Ten sections. §III finds that the sentence under withdrawal is the only one to have survived every stage of the proceedings intact, and proposes that this is a property of correction rather than of robustness: to remove a proposition the record repeatedly reproduces it, and each denial increases the number of available specimens. §IV shows that the chronological correction CREATED the field it was meant to close — before it, an implausible attribution; after it, a predecessor, a successor, an interval and a disputed account of transmission, so that the chronology supplied the field's first syllabus. §V distinguishes three hypotheses about the absent original — a lost work reconstructed from its reception, an unwritten work assembled from its corrections, and a work whose composition consists in becoming the object those corrections require — and declines to print three separate books. §VI observes that the proceedings have been conducted entirely among the surviving parties, the absent supplying the subject, the evidence and the occasion for disagreement while remaining ineligible to amend the minutes, and that the committee recognizes this as standard practice without being able to resolve it. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

methodology: The instrument suspends a retraction before its proposal, on grounds discovered after the retraction was proposed and before the proposal occurred. Its sections proceed by identifying, in each prior document of the sequence, the operation that document performed rather than the one it described. Its disposition preserves every version and forbids silent substitution, so that a future reader can determine when the author became aware of each difficulty and what he published afterward.
falsification_conditions: The instrument makes one empirical claim and it is falsifiable: that a proposition circulated only through its own corrections accumulates specimens rather than losing them, so that denial increases availability. This predicts a measurable asymmetry between claims withdrawn and claims never made, testable in any citation record. §VIII makes a second, methodological claim which the archive's own capture registry can test: that a reader primed with a destination is not an independent witness to it — measurable as the difference between primed and unprimed retrieval, which the registry records at 382 captures under the Reception Apparatus Protocol. The instrument is void if the book it documents does not appear.

wiki_article: The Protoretrocausal Meta-Erratum, deposit #1600 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (8 September 2026), is the third instrument in the erratum sequence and the one that makes the book possible. It suspends the pending retraction of the anticipatory erratum at #1598, effective prior to that retraction's proposal, on the discovery that the erratum had performed the publication whose consequences it claimed merely to anticipate: to withdraw an interpretation intelligibly, the withdrawal had to supply it in enough detail to be cited, disputed, misunderstood and independently rediscovered. The erratum was the first edition. The term is glossed exactly — proto- for the stage before the cause has been adequately formulated, retrocausal for the subsequent discovery that this stage was already consequential, meta- to indicate that responsibility has been transferred to the apparatus — and disclaims any physical reading: it describes the administratively familiar circumstance in which a later document determines what an earlier document will always have meant. The date remains unchanged; the past acquires a footnote. Its most consequential finding is that the chronological correction created the field it was meant to close: before it, an implausible attribution; after it, a predecessor, a successor, an interval and a disputed account of transmission, the chronology having supplied the field's first syllabus. Its most exposed is §VIII, which records that readers instructed where to arrive reached the conclusion before the argument and that their arrival was mistaken for independent confirmation — a reader told where to arrive is not an independent witness to the existence of the destination. That is a methodological claim the archive's own capture registry can test, and it is entered as testable. The disposition preserves every version and forbids silent substitution, so that a future reader can determine when the author became aware of each difficulty and what he published afterward.

defines_concepts.definition: Of a document: issued at the stage before its cause has been adequately formulated (proto-), later found to have been already consequential at that stage (retrocausal), with responsibility for the finding transferred to the apparatus rather than the author (meta-). It makes no claim about physical time. It describes the circumstance in which a later document determines what an earlier document will always have meant: the date remains unchanged and the past acquires a footnote.

The finding that a withdrawal intelligible enough to be understood must supply the interpretation it withdraws in sufficient detail to be cited, disputed, misunderstood and independently rediscovered — and has therefore performed the publication it claimed to anticipate. The erratum is the first edition.

The condition of the parties an inquiry is about, who supply its subject, its evidence and its occasion for disagreement while being unable to contest any of it. Recognized as standard practice in every discipline that studies the dead, and not resolved by being recognized.

The distinction between a reader who arrives at a conclusion having been told where to arrive and a reader who finds one. The first is not an independent witness to the existence of the destination; the first may nevertheless discover something there, and any such discovery must be recorded separately from the itinerary.
